headline: ADP printed 38k into two-thirds odds of a hike. The curve sat still Wednesday and rate vol rose anyway.
stance: Two-thirds of a hike is priced for the FOMC, Sep 16, and the labor data keeps missing. Wednesday settled nothing: no yield moved, MOVE rose a fourth day, and Friday's payrolls now carries the meeting.

news.head: ADP 38,000, slowest since January
news.body: August private payrolls +38k against +47k expected, July revised up to 46k. Manufacturing, professional services and information all shed jobs.

news.head: Yen up a second day on Takata
news.body: USD/JPY 156.80 (~5am ET). BoJ's Takata said the bank should drop its 0.25%-every-six-months pace. ING flags intervention talk.

news.head: Broadcom guided Q4 to $34.8bn
news.body: Reported after Wednesday's close. Q3 revenue $29.59bn, +86% y/y, ahead of $29.4bn. Q4 guide is +93% y/y, with operating margin near 66%.

news.head: Crude lower for the first time since the Hormuz strike
news.body: WTI $89.94, -1.2% (~4:15am ET), from $90.76 at Wednesday's close. Crude closed in the 92nd percentile of three years for a third session.

implications: A 38k ADP and a two-thirds-priced hike cannot both be right. Friday's payrolls settles it, and the rates market has one session of vol to carry until then.
The yen is moving on the BoJ, not on the dollar. A hawkish BoJ alongside a hawkish Fed takes the funding leg out of every carry trade at once.

watch.head: Jobless claims, 8:30
watch.body: Running near 203k. ADP already missed, so an uptick the day before the jobs report is the harder of the two signals.

watch.head: ISM services, 10:00
watch.body: The survey half that has held up. With a hike two-thirds priced, a strong number reads hawkish rather than good.

watch.head: Unit labor costs, 8:30
watch.body: The wage input. ADP has job-stayer pay at 3.0% y/y and job-changers at 4.7%, which is not the acceleration a hike needs.

watch.head: USD/JPY and the intervention line
watch.body: Second straight session of yen strength on BoJ comments alone. Watch whether Tokyo follows the words with anything.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The whole curve sat still Wednesday and MOVE rose anyway, a fourth straight day and the highest since Aug 3.
Vol without yield movement is hedging into Friday, not repricing. The front end did its repricing Monday and Tuesday.
A 38k ADP makes this a wage question. Job-stayer pay ran 3.0% y/y in August, job-changers 4.7% — no acceleration to hike into.
sections.positioning: Spec net length in 2-year Treasuries has sat at the 100th percentile of three years for five weeks. A standing extended long, into a meeting the market prices as a hike.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Breadth stopped falling. The share of S&P names above their 50-day rose Wednesday for the first time in five sessions.
Broadcom's Q4 guide is +93% y/y and it still needs 66% margins to hold. The AI capex names are being marked on the guide now, not the beat.
Downside hedges came off into the jobs report, not on. Skew and the VIX curve both unwound Tuesday's bid.
sections.positioning: Spec positioning in Russell 2000 has been at the 2nd percentile of three years for eighteen weeks. A standing extended short in small caps, unmoved by the hike repricing.

single_name.note: BayCom, a small commercial bank, joined the insider-buy list Wednesday. Two insider rules fired, it trades above its 200-day, 4.0 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HYG/LQD rose Wednesday, the first up day in six. The ratio led the cash marks wider, so it has to lead them back.
Syndicated loan yields rose a third straight session to 7.18%. Loans reprice with the front end faster than bonds do.
The reverse repo facility is empty and reserves sit at $2.92tn. A Treasury cash build from here drains reserves directly.
sections.positioning: Dealer high-yield inventory fell another six points last week, to the 6th percentile of three years. Dealers are not warehousing the widening.
